quotes.quote: If you would like, you may compress your Sitemap files using gzip to reduce your bandwidth requirement
however the sitemap file once uncompressed must be no larger than 50MB
each Sitemap file that you provide must have no more than 50,000 URLs and must be no larger than 50MB (52,428,800 bytes)
Sitemap index files may not list more than 50,000 Sitemaps and must be no larger than 50MB (52,428,800 bytes) and can be compressed
This location can be a Sitemap, an Atom file, RSS file or a simple text file.
You can provide an RSS (Real Simple Syndication) 2.0 or Atom 0.3 or 1.0 feed.
<link> field - indicates the URL
modified date field (the <pubDate> field for RSS feeds and the <updated> date for Atom feeds)
Use of the modified date field is optional.
The text file must have one URL per line. The URLs cannot contain embedded new lines.
You must fully specify URLs, including the http.
Each text file can contain a maximum of 50,000 URLs and must be no larger than 50MB (52,428,800 bytes).
The text file must use UTF-8 encoding.
The text file should contain no information other than the list of URLs.
The text file should contain no header or footer information.
If you would like, you may compress your Sitemap text file using gzip to reduce your bandwidth requirement.
These have the fixed values ID1 = 31 (0x1f, \037), ID2 = 139 (0x8b, \213), to identify the file as being in gzip format.
This contains a Cyclic Redundancy Check value of the uncompressed data computed according to CRC-32 algorithm
This contains the size of the original (uncompressed) input data modulo 2^32.
A compliant decompressor must check ID1, ID2, and CM, and provide an error indication if any of these have incorrect values.
The "href" attribute contains the link's IRI. atom:link elements MUST have an href attribute, whose value MUST be a IRI reference
a Date construct indicating the most recent instant in time when an entry or feed was modified
Publishers MAY change the value of this element over time.
A Date construct is an element whose content MUST conform to the "date-time" production in [RFC3339].
atom:entry elements MUST contain exactly one atom:updated element.
You can name the text file anything you wish.
You can name the text file anything you wish. Please check to make sure that your URLs follow the RFC-3986 standard for URIs
